definition: goose is an open-source artificial intelligence agent originally developed by Block.
details: It runs locally as a desktop application or command-line interface and can perform software development and other computer-based tasks using large language models. goose supports models from multiple providers, including Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Amazon Bedrock, and OpenRouter, and locally hosted models through Ollama.

explainer.lead: Goose is an open-source AI agent, originally developed by Block, that uses large language models to carry out software-development and other computer-based tasks. It runs on your own computer as a desktop application or command-line interface, with a choice of hosted or locally hosted models.

tiers.eli5: Goose is like a computer helper that you can ask to do jobs such as helping with software. It lives in an app or a text-based window on your computer, and you can choose which AI brain powers it. That brain can come from an online provider or run locally through Ollama.
tiers.practitioner: Run goose through its desktop application or CLI, then connect a supported model from Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Amazon Bedrock, OpenRouter, or a locally hosted model through Ollama. It can then be applied to software-development and other computer-based tasks. Running the agent locally does not itself make the model local; that depends on the selected provider or Ollama setup.
tiers.paperLevel: Goose can be described as an open-source agent A = (I, M, T), where I is a locally running desktop or command-line interface, M is a selected LLM, and T is the set of software-development and other computer-based tasks it performs. Model choice spans several hosted providers and locally hosted models through Ollama; local execution of the agent should therefore be distinguished from local model inference.

explainer.example: A developer opens goose in the command line, selects a locally hosted model through Ollama, and asks it to help fix a software bug. Goose runs on the developer's computer and uses that model to work on the development task.

usedIn.name: Software development
usedIn.detail: Uses a selected large language model to perform development tasks from a local desktop app or CLI.

usedIn.name: Computer-based tasks
usedIn.detail: Can apply large language models to other tasks on a computer beyond software development.

explainer.intuition: Goose is a local control point for an AI agent: you give it a task, choose the language model behind it, and let it work on computer-based tasks without being tied to one model provider.
howItWorks: Run goose locally as a desktop application or command-line interface.
Select a model from a supported provider or a locally hosted model through Ollama.
Give goose a software-development or other computer-based task.
Goose uses the selected large language model to perform the task.
explainer.whyItMatters: Its open-source, locally running interfaces and support for multiple model providers give users flexibility in how they deploy an AI agent. Ollama support also allows the language model itself to be hosted locally.
misconceptions: Goose is an AI agent, not a large language model itself.
Running goose locally does not necessarily mean the selected model runs locally.
It is not restricted to models from a single provider.

diagram.caption: Goose runs locally and connects a user's task to either a hosted provider or a locally hosted Ollama model.
